candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0106.

options.A: You are exempt from iPLEDGE because FDA ended the isotretinoin pregnancy-safety program when it approved program changes in February 2026.
options.B: Isotretinoin remains under iPLEDGE for embryo-fetal risk; current program safeguards still apply, including FDA-authorized pregnancy-testing flexibilities.
options.C: Only a pregnancy test after the final dose is required because FDA eliminated pretreatment pregnancy testing for every patient starting isotretinoin in 2026.
options.D: iPLEDGE applies only to patients who report current sexual activity; documented abstinence automatically removes pregnancy-testing and program requirements.

candidate.rationale: As of August 14, 2026, iPLEDGE remains in effect to mitigate embryo-fetal risk. FDA delayed implementation of the approved 2026 modifications to November 15, 2026, and until implementation is complete FDA continues its stated enforcement discretion for certain pregnancy-testing requirements. The absence of current sexual activity does not mean the iPLEDGE program itself no longer applies.
candidate.source_claim_supported: FDA iPLEDGE REMS page, June 16, 2026 update: implementation of approved modifications delayed to November 15, 2026; until full implementation FDA continues stated enforcement discretion regarding certain pregnancy-testing requirements. Reviewed 2026-08-14.

candidate.stem: A client who can become pregnant is starting isotretinoin and says, “I am not sexually active, so the pregnancy-prevention program does not apply to me.” Which response is most accurate in August 2026?
